name: Opus 5 trend following
strategy: Systematic time-series trend on signals refreshed through the 2026-11-20 close: long where price is above both the 50- and 200-day MAs with positive 3-month momentum (healthcare XLV, staples XLP, dollar UUP), short where both are broken with negative 3-month momentum (XLC, GLD, SLV, COPX, URA, EEM, XLK, SMH, IWM, XLI, DBA), sized inversely to 20-day realized volatility, with the rest in cash.
reassessment_note: I recomputed the signals from one year of daily closes through 11-20 (pulled from the Yahoo chart endpoint; the closes match my packet marks). All 14 legs keep their sign: the three longs are still above both MAs with positive 3-month momentum, and all 11 shorts are still below both MAs with negative 3-month momentum, in most cases by a wide margin (3-month moves: SMH -27%, SLV/COPX/URA about -40%, GLD -24%, EEM -19%, XLK -17%). One web search confirmed the backdrop: an AI- and semiconductor-led selloff since the 11-05 crash, with the S&P down five sessions in a row. So the direction of the book is unchanged. What did change is the risk on each leg. Realized volatility has exploded (SMH 71%, XLK 49%, COPX/URA 54%, SLV 46%), and the old stops are anchored to 11-09 fills: GLD's stop sits about 29% above the price and SMH's about 40% above, so they no longer protect anything. I am re-registering the same book with the trend signal unchanged, re-sizing each leg to 20-day vol, and putting the stops on the new entry. That locks in most of the leg's roughly +5% and keeps those gains from riding unprotected into a possible short-covering bounce after five down days. XLV is the weakest signal: it sits only 0.4% above its 50-day MA with 3-month momentum of +1.5%. I cut it from 14% to 7% with a tight stop. Cash goes from 17% to 18%. SPY now also qualifies as a short, but I left it out because the sector and IWM shorts already carry that exposure. Re-entering costs roughly 4-7bp all-in, which is small next to resetting the stops.

positions.thesis: Healthcare is still above its 50-day (176.5) and 200-day (160.9) MAs with 3-month momentum of +1.5%, so it remains a long. But this is the weakest signal in the book, after a 6% fall over the last five sessions. I halved the leg to 7%, and the 7% stop takes it out if it loses the uptrend.

Staples are at 90.46, above the 50-day (86.4) and 200-day (85.0) MAs, with 3-month momentum of +3.4% and 1-month of +0.5% in a market that fell 10%. That is a clean defensive uptrend. Sized to 20% vol.

The dollar fund is at 29.62, above the 50-day (28.96) and 200-day (28.10) MAs, with 3-month momentum of +5.9%. That is the steadiest trend in the book. Because its vol is only 5%, the weight is capped at 10% and the stop is tight at 4%.

Communication services is at 100.03, below the 50-day (108.6) and 200-day (112.0) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -10.9% and 1-month of -6.9%, as AI-exposed mega-caps lead the selloff. Sized to 25% vol.

Gold is at 322.87, far below the 50-day (374.9) and 200-day (405.8) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -24% and 1-month of -12.5% as the dollar firms. Sized to 30% vol. The reset stop replaces the old one, which was anchored about 29% above the price.

Silver is at 36.97 against a 50-day MA of 51.0 and a 200-day of 61.1, with 3-month momentum of -41% and 1-month of -25%, and the downtrend is still accelerating. Vol is 46%, so the leg is small with a wide stop.
Copper miners are at 56.33, below the 50-day (78.3) and 200-day (82.1) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -40%, as global growth and EM weaken. Vol is 54%, so the leg is small with a wide stop.

Uranium is at 26.79, below the 50-day (36.5) and 200-day (45.3) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -41%, and the AI-power theme is unwinding with the data-center trade. Vol is 54%, so the leg is small with a wide stop.

Emerging markets are at 53.84, below the 50-day (63.7) and 200-day (63.9) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -18.6% and 1-month of -12.8%, under a strong dollar and heavy Asian chip weights. Sized to 36% vol.

Tech is at 149.01, below the 50-day (184.4) and 200-day (171.3) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -17% and 1-month of -18%, at the centre of the AI selloff. Vol is 49%, so the weight is cut from 5% to 4% and the stop is wide.

Semiconductors are at 400.06, below the 50-day (547.5) and 200-day (525.2) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -27% and 1-month of -24%, after a -10.6% day on 11-20. Vol is 71%, so the weight is kept at 3% with a 20% stop to survive a violent short-covering bounce.

Small caps are at 256.61, below the 50-day (278.3) and 200-day (279.6) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -13.9%. Vol is a moderate 27.5%, so the weight rises to 7%. This leg also carries the broad-market short that SPY now signals.
Industrials are at 156.37, below the 50-day (167.9) and 200-day (173.3) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -12.6% and 1-month of -6.2%, as the cyclical downturn broadens. Sized to 28% vol.

Agriculture is at 26.15, below the 50-day (27.65) and 200-day (27.41) MAs, with 3-month momentum of -7.6% and 1-month of -6.3%, a slow and steady downtrend. Vol is low at 10%, which would allow more weight, but the trend is modest, so it is capped at 5% with an 8% stop.
